Markus — see proposed language below (included as text for quick copy/paste into the redline):

--- proposed Section 4 (Data Transfers) snippet ---
"For transfers of personal data from the EEA/UK to third countries, the parties shall rely on the European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two) and where applicable the UK International Data Transfer Addendum. Redwood will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures (including encryption at rest and in transit, key management with customer-controlled KMS options, and role-based access controls)."

--- proposed Subprocessor notification clause ---
"Redwood will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior notice of the addition or material change to any Subprocessor. Customer may object in writing on reasonable grounds relating to data protection; upon receipt of an objection, the parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve the objection within thirty (30) days. If the parties cannot resolve the objection, Customer may require suspension of the applicable processing activities for the affected data subject to the parties' mutual agreement on an alternative arrangement."

Notes: 1) This avoids an automatic opt-out but preserves a remediation path customers often request. 2) For high-risk processors (e.g., cross-border logging providers, bespoke analytics), we should be prepared to discuss mitigation (logging redaction, dedicated tenancy, or contractual limits). 3) We should offer to include our subprocessor list URL and a process for early notice (email + portal).

Also: counsel asked about specific evidence for SCCs — prepare SOC2 Type II plus a short transfer impact assessment summary. I'll draft a short paragraph to insert in the redline offering those exhibits.

Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
